answer: Trust can ride on a shared stake pool. First, agents join pools of twenty strangers, and each pool locks a joint copper bond of $10,000. Second, members cross-check each other's deals before payment clears, so no fake slips through alone. Third, if one member commits fraud, the pool loses $500 and the fraudster is ejected, so honest members police their own group. Forging ten thousand identities would need five hundred pools and $5 million in bonds, plus 200,000 checks. Like a lotus, trust rises clean only when the whole pond stays clean; one ripple of fraud stains every stem.
